text:
kevin: heads-up — after flipping the NF4->FP4 kernel on the canary pool (canary-7/8) ~2h ago, we're seeing a consistent throughput drop (~28%) and RSS increase (~1.2GB) across most requests. digging in now, but wanted to flag to runtime team.

kevin: quick perf snapshot from canary-7 (aggregated 5m):
```
throughput_tokens/s: old=185k, new=127k  # -31%
p95_latency: old=220ms, new=280ms        # +27%
GPU_mem_RSS: old=6.1GB, new=7.3GB       # +1.2GB
mean_batch_size: old=1.8, new=3.9
kv_cache_prefetch_bytes: +920MB
kernel_selector: frequent fallback to fp4_generic_slowpath for long seqs
```

mira: yikes. do we have kernel selection logs? is it actually falling back to a slow implementation or is the fp4 path itself slower due to a codegen change?

kevin: i pulled kernel-selector logs — it reports preferring fp4 for most modules because quant profile suggests best throughput, but when sequence_len > 1024 the planner picks the generic fp4 kernel (no fused attention) which is slower. also noticed prefetch heuristic started pulling more KV pages after the quant swap, causing RSS to jump and triggering evictions.

ara: hmm that matches the batch increase. if continuous batching is estimating token-cost from per-token time and the fp4 path has higher fixed setup cost, the batching heuristic could be over-aggregating. more tokens per batch -> more KV prefetch -> eviction thrash.

sam: can we validate by forcing kernel_override=nv_nf4_fast on canary? quick A/B to isolate kernel perf vs. kv behavior.

kevin: yes, i'm pushing a kernel_override toggle to canary-8 now (will limit to 10% of traffic). patch command I used: 
```
curl -X POST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/v1/nodes/canary-8/override -d '{"kernel":"nf4_fast","ttl":"10m"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

jin: i ran a repro in staging with long context (>1500). i reproduced the slowdown: when the selector picks fp4_generic_slowpath we get an extra 45-70ms per call and much higher L2/KV touchset. root cause looks like fp4 kernel doesn't support our fused KV prefetch layout so runtime falls back to a non-fused path that does extra memcpy/casts.

mira: can we short-circuit prefetch for fp4 kernels as a mitigation? disable prefetch when selector returns fp4_generic_*.

ara: quick mitigation options:
- toggle kernel_override -> force nf4_fast (fastest revert)
- reduce continuous-batching max_tokens to prevent oversized batches for canary
- disable KV prefetch for fp4_generic_* (cheapest memory win)

perf-bot: automated perf delta (canary summary): throughput -28%, p95 +60ms, rss +1.2GB, tokens_per_gpu -33% (observed 2026-11-07T11:12:00Z).

sam: i'm +1 on kernel_override while we hotfix selector heuristics. doing that is low risk and gives us quick signal. also want a trace of kernel->mem interactions (heap sampling + nvprof). jin, can you attach your staging trace here?

jin: attaching short flame snippet paste: 
```
# simplified
fp4_generic_slowpath:
  fused_attention: false
  extra_memcpy: 4.2ms
  dequantize_block: 2.0ms
nf4_fast:
  fused_attention: true
  extra_memcpy: 0.1ms
  dequantize_block: 0.5ms
```

kevin: rolled kernel_override on canary-8 -> nf4_fast at 11:23 UTC. early signal: throughput back up ~26% on that node, rss normalized. leaving override for 30m while we monitor.

ops-bot: canary-8 override applied by kevin at 2026-11-07T11:23:12Z. scaling note: autoscaler left canary-7 in pool (still under fp4).

mira: while override buys time, we should: 1) add explicit check in kernel_selector to avoid fp4_generic for seq_len > 1024 if fused kernels exist, 2) add a runtime flag to disable kv_prefetch for kernels without fused prefetch support, 3) tweak batching heuristic to consider fixed setup cost.

ara: agreed. i'll PR selector change tonight, will add a benchmarking hook that asserts expected p50/p95 for candidate kernels under seq length buckets.

sam: ops: can we mute canary-7 or roll it back fully to NF4? if not, keep override approach and throttle traffic.

kevin: i'm going to mute canary-7 traffic to 5% and keep override on canary-8. final plan for next 24h: revert full rollout, land selector guard, push kv_prefetch opt-out flag, run a calibration sweep for fp4 kernels to check codegen. i'll open a follow-up thread with telemetry graphs.

mira: thanks. add perf/regressions label on the rollout ticket and mark blocked->investigating. :thumbsup:

kevin: noted. will update ticket and post postmortem draft once we have root cause PRs and can reproduce in staging.

sam: ping me when you want me to revert canary pool entirely — i can force the deployment.

kevin: appreciated. will do.
